headline: Run 1’s eight fixes hold, and the scheduler, relay, health and backups behave right end to end through the real Worker. One Major remains: the relay’s own auth checks have no test. Five Minors: a suspended person’s job would make the scheduler tick every minute (D141), the stamp stays away for 30 s when a screen opens with the relay down (from run 1’s fix 6), and Windows tooling gaps hid eight breakage checks and every metrics confirmation.

suites.db: pgTAP 216 ok; API 125 pass, 7 skipped; route sweep green
suites.e2e: 1397 pass; lived 24 pass; server 4 pass; QA flows 12 of 12 run, FLOW-R2-3 fails its stamp step
suites.mutants: 39 of 52 killed, 5 survived, 8 stale (all 8 killed with LF)

findings.title: The relay’s own guards have no test: posting a hint without the secret, or opening a channel without a pass, stays green
findings.detail: Nothing imports `apps/worker/src/index.ts` or `channel.ts` in any suite; only `clock.ts` is tested. Deleting the relay secret check on `POST /hint`, or replacing `verifyPass()` on `/connect` with the raw query value, leaves every suite green. By hand (wrangler dev) the Worker behaves correctly today, so this is a guard nobody holds, not a hole. The relay is the realtime privacy boundary (D100).
findings.evidence:
| `relay-hint-no-secret` | unit | **SURVIVED** |
| `relay-connect-no-pass` | unit | **SURVIVED** |
By hand: hint no bearer: 401 {"code":"signed_out",...}; A’s signature on B’s channel: refused

findings.title: A suspended person’s due one-off job makes the scheduler tick every minute, forever
findings.detail: `jobs_people('once')` skips suspended people, but `jobs_next_once()` doesn’t, so their due job is never run and never leaves `due`. Every tick then answers `next` = now + 1 minute (nextTick clamps a past time), and the Worker wakes the API, and Neon, every minute: the opposite of D141. No path in this build creates it (suspending arrives with B38, and only the admin schedules one-off jobs), so Minor today; Major once members have one-off jobs and can be suspended. The `once` suspended filter is untested too (mutant `once-jobs-for-suspended` survived).
findings.repro: On sen_qa: suspend a person; insert a scheduled_jobs row for them, run_at an hour ago; call runTick() three times

findings.title: With the relay down when a screen opens, the “Updated…” stamp stays away for the first 30 s
findings.detail: Run 1’s fix for finding 6 made the stamp wait for `useLive.updatedAt`, which only the realtime module sets (a hint, a reconnect, or a 30 s poll). A screen that loads normally while the relay is refusing shows no stamp until the first poll, so for 30 s it looks live when it isn’t. The live-stamp comment says “once the screen has loaded”; the screen’s own load isn’t what it reads. Run 1’s FLOW-2 (15 s timeout) would now fail.
findings.repro: qa/e2e: playwright test -c b06r2.config.ts -g FLOW-R2-3 (relay sockets closed by routeWebSocket)

findings.title: On Windows every multi-line breakage check is “stale”, so eight guards (three of them run 1’s fixes) went unjudged
findings.detail: The repo has `* text=auto` and Git for Windows checks the mutants worktree out with CRLF, so a `find` holding `\n` never matches. The sweep reported 8 stale; re-run with `core.eol=lf` all 8 are killed, so the guards hold, but `mutants.mjs` on this laptop silently skips them. Run 1’s finding 5 is only partly fixed.

findings.title: On Windows qa-diff never confirms a flag, yet its report says each was measured three times
findings.detail: The confirm step passes `-g "\sask$|\srefund$"` to pnpm through cmd.exe, which reads `|` as a pipe, so it exits 255 without measuring; both flags reached the ledger as single samples while the report text says “measured twice more”. The base API run also failed (main’s pgTAP: relation "scheduled_jobs" does not exist), so no route has main’s numbers. Re-measured by hand, three each side: both flags are noise (finding 9 for the standing one).

findings.title: A person can register any number of push tokens, and every push loops over all of them
findings.detail: `PUT /push/token` has no cap per person and no rate limit. 300 made-up tokens were all stored; `fcmPusher.send` calls FCM once per token. Harmless today (only the admin is pushed), but the first slice that pushes members inherits it.
findings.repro: signed in as a member, PUT /api/push/token {token: "bulk-<i>"} for i in 0..299
findings.evidence: member registered 300 of 300 made-up tokens; rows: [ { n: 300 } ]

findings.title: A plain Sign out leaves the phone’s push token on the server unless the app’s own DELETE gets through
findings.detail: D142 (5) says sign-out deletes the token. The web app sends `DELETE /push/token` first, racing it against 3 s; the server’s `/auth/sign-out` deletes nothing (only `revoke-sessions` does). If that DELETE fails, the signed-out phone keeps the person’s pushes until someone else signs in on it.
findings.repro: POST /api/auth/sign-out with a session whose phone registered a token, without the DELETE
findings.evidence:
POST /auth/sign-out (phone-2, no DELETE first): { status: 200 }
admin tokens after a plain sign-out: [ ..., { fcm_token: 'phone-2' }, ... ]

findings.title: Opening the Insights tab takes about 2.5 s to settle, with a see-through frame and two different skeletons (standing: main does the same)
findings.detail: The eyes pass called `ask/3` wrong: a see-through frame of Home behind skeleton bars, then two skeletons, the first without the app bar. The flag (2908 vs 455 ms) was a single base sample; re-measured three times each side, main settles in 2490–2582 ms and the branch in 2522–2698 ms, so B06 didn’t cause it. A standing item; follow-up: the tab’s first frame should be its own skeleton with its app bar.
findings.repro: pnpm --filter @sen/web exec playwright test -c e2e/diff.config.ts --project metrics-head --repeat-each 3 -g "ask$" e2e/journeys.spec.ts (and metrics-base)

findings.title: An open relay socket outlives its pass and Sign out everywhere
findings.detail: The pass is checked only when connecting; the Channel never closes sockets. A lost phone with Sen open keeps receiving topic-only hints (no data) until it disconnects. D100 keeps data out of hints, so this is only “something changed” timing.
findings.evidence: Channel.fetch accepts; nothing closes on expiry or revoke

findings.title: The scheduler functions’ guard is “no user id set”, so an empty id lists everyone
findings.detail: `jobs_people()`, `jobs_next_once()` and `jobs_health()` refuse a request that has a user id; app_user with `app.user_id = ''` gets every person’s id. No route runs that way today; it rests on the API never running a person’s request without their id.
findings.repro: begin; set local role app_user; select set_config('app.user_id','',true); select * from jobs_people('daily');
